Plaza for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, macOS 11 or newer)

Install: drag Plaza into the Applications folder.

First launch: Plaza isn't notarized by Apple yet, so macOS blocks the first open with
"Plaza can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software" (or
"Apple could not verify Plaza is free of malware").

  macOS 14 and older: in Applications, right-click (or Control-click) Plaza, choose Open,
  then click Open in the dialog.
  macOS 15 and newer: double-click Plaza once and click Done. Then open System Settings >
  Privacy & Security, scroll down to "Plaza was blocked", click Open Anyway, and confirm
  with your password or Touch ID.

macOS remembers the choice; after that Plaza opens normally.

Turn your volume down before the first note: long reverb tails and stacked chords get loud fast.

Keys: Z-M and Q-I play two octaves, [ ] or Left/Right change octave, Up/Down change preset,
Tab toggles slow + pitch down, Esc releases every note. Cmd shortcuts (Cmd-Q, Cmd-H) work as
usual. USB MIDI keyboards connect by themselves. Recordings (REC) go to Music/Plaza in your
home folder; the music-note button opens it in Finder.

Free and open source: https://github.com/nunyabiz765/plaza
From Center Point Labs: https://centerpointlabs.dev/services/plaza/
